This tutorial introduces to data augmentation with the package `housepi`. We'll walk through the process of associating augmented variable to individuals to then proceed with standard model generation and inference. 

## Estimate Incubation Periods Distribution

For simplicity, we start testing data augmentation on a database which is not a household survey. Instead we consider a simulated report documenting the days when a number of cases were exposed to infection and the days of symptom onset.

Assuming the incubation period to be described by a gamma distribution, we want to estimate the respective parameters augmenting the exposure and onset times, modeled as uniformly distributed in the reported ranges. 
We associate a positive status to all individuals and we correct for right censoring modifying the maximum values as follows:

```{r}
delays <- read.csv("delays.csv")
delays[["exposure_max"]] <- delays[["exposure_max"]] + 1 - 1e-5
delays[["onset_max"]] <- delays[["onset_max"]] + 1 - 1e-5
delays[["status"]] <- 1
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(delays))
```

We generate the model as showed in the [walkthrough](walkthrough.html):

```{r}
# generate the model
hemi_1 <- housepi::generate_model("example_augm_delay_incubation")

# gamma distribution parameter definitions
par_1 <- housepi::ParameterFrame(list(
  shape = list(x = 1, 
               prior = "unif", args = list(min = 0, max = 5),
               rule = "norm", rule_args = list(sd = 1)),
  scale = list(x = 1,
               prior = "unif", args = list(min = 0, max = 5),
               rule = "norm", rule_args = list(sd = 1))
  ))

# general setup
setup_1 <- list(num_iter = 100000, num_adapt = 2500, burn_in = 5000,
              thinning = 10, seed = 4815162342, num_chains = 1)

# associate data, parameters and setup
housepi::build_model(hemi_1, data = delays, params = par_1$df, setup = setup_1)
```


The warning is telling us that the database has been interpreted as composed of single individuals, i .e. living in separate households.

### Build Augmented Variables

Similarly to parameter definitions, for augmented variables we provide a DataFrame or a file with the models and proposer rules needed for the Bayesian Monte Carlo. However, augmented variable definitions are more delicate, since they can depend on data or parameters. We state which value should be imported from data formatting it as a string "<value-name>`@D`". Here we associate to each individual an exposure and an onset time.

```{r}
augm_1 <- housepi::AugmentedFrame(list(
  # define 'exposure' time
  exposure = list(
    x = "exposure_min@D", # start from data 'exposure_min'
    model = "unif",                      # associate a uniform model
    args = list(min = "exposure_min@D",  # within the range 'exposure_min' 
                max = "exposure_max@D"), # and 'exposure_max'
    rule = "norm",              # choose normal rule for the Monte Carlo
    rule_args = list(sd = 0.25) # with a std. dev. of 0.25
  ),
  
  # define 'onset' time
  onset = list(
    x = "onset_max@D", # start from 'onset_max'
    model = "unif",    # ...
    args = list(min = "onset_min@D", 
                max = "onset_max@D"),
    rule = "norm",
    rule_args = list(sd = 0.25)
  )
))

# associate augmented variable definitions
housepi::build_model(hemi_1, augm = augm_1$df)
```

We run the inference and we extract the results

```{r}
mcmc_trace_1 <- housepi::run_inference(hemi_1)
plot(mcmc_trace_1, col="#0E86D4")
results_1 <- summary(mcmc_trace_1)
```

## Augment Onset Times

We use the template model "augm_onset_single_intr", where surveys are conditioned on single introduction and follow the times of onset.

```{r}
hemi_2 <- housepi::generate_model("augm_onset_single_intr")
```
This time we load the parameter definitions directly from the model template:

```{r}
par_2 <- housepi::ParameterFrame(housepi_model = hemi_2)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(par_2$df))
```

We propose the following augmented variable definitions

```{r}
augm_2 <- housepi::AugmentedFrame()

# add 'onset_date' definition
augm_2$add(name = "onset_date", 
           x = 0,
           rule = "norm", rule_args = list(sd = 0.25),
           range = list(min = -3))

# add 'incub_period' definition
augm_2$add(name = "incub_period", 
           init_rand = TRUE,
           model = "gamma", 
           args = list(shape = "inc_shape@P", 
                       scale = "inc_scale@P"),
           rule = "model", 
           range = list(min = 0, max = 14))

# assign model arguments of incubation period from parameters
# we use the inferred values from the first example
par_2$add(name = "inc_shape", x = results_1$statistics["shape", "Mean"])
par_2$add(name = "inc_scale", x = results_1$statistics["scale", "Mean"])
```

```{r}

setup_2 <- list(num_iter = 30000, num_adapt = 2500, burn_in = 2000,
              thinning = 25, seed = 576125013)

housepi::build_model(hemi_2, data = "survey.csv", params = par_2$df, 
                     setup = setup_2, augm = augm_2$df)
```

### Simulate an Outbreak

We run a simulation with the method `simulate`.

```{r}
# override status of the dataset according to simulation 
hemi_2$simulate()

# store the simulated dataset
database <- hemi_2$data()

# show the results of the simulation 
head(database[c("status", "incub_period", "onset_date")])
```

We can see that in addition to the status, the simulation also associates the values of the augmented variables: the incubation period and the onset time.

### Simulate an Outbreak

As a sanity check, we can verify that inference returns the parameters used for the simulation.

```{r}
mcmc_trace <- housepi::run_inference(hemi2)
coda::traceplot(mcmc_trace)
results <- summary(mcmc_trace)

# collect the information for the check
inames <- params[params["infer"] == TRUE, "name"]
data.frame(Expec = params[params["infer"] == TRUE, "value"],
           Mean = results[["statistics"]][inames, "Mean"],
           Q2.5 = results[["quantiles"]][inames, "2.5%"],
           Q97.5 = results[["quantiles"]][inames, "97.5%"])
```

Remember that templated models do not simulate the sampling process.

```{r}
p <- housepi::ParameterFrame(dget("parameters"))
```
